findings.summary: Solid Rock and Rindo Berry were omitted, so Spark was predicted at 24-30 but dealt 19 and first Razor Leaf was predicted at 40-52 but dealt 15.
findings.observed_fact: RAM verified ability 116 and held item 553; battle text verified Rindo consumption.
findings.strategic_judgment: The shared damage model could change KO timing and therefore recommendations; scorer v10 now applies Solid Rock to super-effective hits and Rindo to super-effective Grass hits.
findings.next_test: Require the Tirtouga regressions and full battle suites to stay green.
findings.state_unavailable_reason: No per-turn savestate was captured; the terminal state cannot replay Tirtouga. Exact RAM states remain in the transaction log and focused formula regressions reproduce both observed bounds.

findings.summary: I overrode the scorer with a Croakatoa switch based on type intuition, then spent fresh Fake Out into Protect and absorbed Acid plus Water Pulse before returning to the scorer line.
findings.observed_fact: Croakatoa fell from 46 to 12 HP; the later certified Ohmnomnom pivot survived and finished Skrelp.
findings.strategic_judgment: This is not a proven dominated branch without a replay, so it must not become a classifier rule; future overrides need deterministic evidence stronger than type intuition.
findings.next_test: Use the history-aware classifier without manual override in the next comparable fresh-entry matchup.

findings.summary: One fresh-entry Fake Out PP was consumed into known Protect priority without producing damage or flinch.
findings.observed_fact: Protect acted before Fake Out and PP dropped from 5 to 4.
findings.strategic_judgment: The generic Fake Out threshold rule now rejects targets with a known equal-or-higher-priority blocking move.
findings.next_test: Keep the Protect rejection regression green.

correct_choices: Fresh-entry Fake Out into Murkrow dealt 11, denied its turn, and made Spark a guaranteed modeled follow-up KO.
The scorer correctly switched damaged Ohmnomnom to Bushtank against Tirtouga and later selected the razor-thin Ohmnomnom pivot that survived Skrelp and finished first.
No Pokémon fainted and the terminal win was verified from RAM.
